answers.explanation: A program that could reset the timer could keep the CPU forever.
Reading the time harms nobody. Programs do it all the time.
With interrupts off, the timer couldn't take the CPU back.
That would wipe the OS and every other program.
The trap is how user programs ask for OS services, so it has to be allowed in user mode.
If a program could set the mode bit to 0 itself, there'd be no protection at all.
Devices are shared; programs go through the OS with system calls.
The system call is the only legitimate doorway into kernel mode.
Returning to the user program sets user mode, bit 1.
